quotes.text: Workers of the world, unite!
The philosophers have only interpreted the world, in various ways. The point, however, is to change it.
The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.
The proletarians have nothing to lose but their chains. They have a world to win.
From each according to his abilities, to each according to his needs!
Men make their own history, but they do not make it as they please.
quotes.source: The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte (1852)

quotes.text: Religion is the sigh of the oppressed creature, the heart of a heartless world, and the soul of soulless conditions. It is the opium of the people.
quotes.source: A Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right (1844)

quotes.text: Capital is dead labour, that, vampire-like, only lives by sucking living labour, and lives the more, the more labour it sucks.
It is not the consciousness of men that determines their being, but, on the contrary, their social being that determines their consciousness.
quotes.source: A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy, Preface (1859)

quotes.text: All that is solid melts into air, all that is holy is profaned.
Freedom is the recognition of necessity.
quotes.source: Anti-Dühring (1878), stating Hegel's view: "freedom is the insight into necessity"

quotes.text: Freedom does not consist in any dreamt-of independence from natural laws, but in the knowledge of these laws.
The state is not "abolished". It dies out.
A revolution is certainly the most authoritarian thing there is.
The first class oppression coincides with that of the female sex by the male.
quotes.source: The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State (1884)

quotes.text: In a sense, we have to say that labour created man himself.
quotes.source: The Part Played by Labour in the Transition from Ape to Man (1876)

quotes.text: The state is nothing but a machine for the oppression of one class by another, and indeed in the democratic republic no less than in the monarchy.
quotes.source: Introduction to The Civil War in France (1891)

quotes.text: Do you want to know what this dictatorship looks like? Look at the Paris Commune. That was the Dictatorship of the Proletariat.
quotes.source: Introduction to The Civil War in France (1891)

quotes.text: Just as Darwin discovered the law of development of organic nature, so Marx discovered the law of development of human history.
quotes.source: Speech at the Grave of Karl Marx (1883)

quotes.text: What each individual wills is obstructed by everyone else, and what emerges is something that no one willed.
Without a revolutionary theory there can be no revolutionary movement.
Communism is Soviet government plus the electrification of the whole country.
quotes.source: Speech to the Moscow Gubernia Party Conference (1920)

quotes.text: Freedom in capitalist society always remains about the same as it was in the ancient Greek republics: freedom for the slave-owners.
A newspaper is not only a collective propagandist and a collective agitator, it is also a collective organiser.
No revolution is worth anything unless it can defend itself.
History is moving in zig-zags and by roundabout ways.
You can become a Communist only when you enrich your mind with a knowledge of all the treasures created by mankind.
quotes.source: The Tasks of the Youth Leagues (1920)

quotes.text: One cannot live in society and be free from society.
Victory will belong only to those who have faith in the people, those who are immersed in the life-giving spring of popular creativity.
quotes.source: Speech to the All-Russia Central Executive Committee (4 November 1917)

quotes.text: The oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament!
I hate the indifferent. Indifference is apathy, parasitism, cowardice; it is not life.
Indifference works powerfully in history. It works passively, but it works.
To tell the truth, to arrive together at the truth, is a communist and revolutionary act.
Illusion is the most tenacious weed in the collective consciousness; history teaches, but it has no pupils.
quotes.source: Italy and Spain, L'Ordine Nuovo (11 March 1921)

quotes.text: Instruct yourselves, because we will need all our intelligence. Agitate, because we will need all our enthusiasm. Organise, because we will need all our strength.
I'm a pessimist because of intelligence, but an optimist because of will.
The crisis consists precisely in the fact that the old is dying and the new cannot be born; in this interregnum a great variety of morbid symptoms appear.
All men are intellectuals: but not all men have in society the function of intellectuals.
History is at once freedom and necessity.
Man is a process and, more exactly, the process of his actions.
Life is beautiful. Let the future generations cleanse it of all evil, oppression and violence, and enjoy it to the full.
Learning carries within itself certain dangers because out of necessity one has to learn from one's enemies.
Old age is the most unexpected of all the things that happen to a man.
The old principle: who does not work shall not eat, has been replaced with a new one: who does not obey shall not eat.
A means can be justified only by its end. But the end in its turn needs to be justified.
A sledgehammer breaks glass but forges steel.
quotes.source: We Do Not Change Our Course (1938)

quotes.text: No one yet has learned to drive a locomotive sitting in his study.
Independent character is like independent thought, it cannot be developed without criticism.
The life of a revolutionary would be quite impossible without a certain amount of "fatalism."
Fascism is nothing but capitalist reaction.
Freedom is always and exclusively freedom for the one who thinks differently.
Freedom only for the supporters of the government, only for the members of one party, however numerous they may be, is no freedom at all.
Without general elections, without unrestricted freedom of press and assembly, without a free struggle of opinion, life dies out in every public institution.
Historically, the errors committed by a truly revolutionary movement are infinitely more fruitful than the infallibility of the cleverest Central Committee.
quotes.source: Organizational Questions of Russian Social Democracy (1904)

quotes.text: The proletarian revolution requires no terror for its aims; it hates and despises killing.
quotes.source: What Does the Spartacus League Want? (1918)

quotes.text: "Order prevails in Berlin!" You foolish lackeys! Your "order" is built on sand.
I was, I am, I shall be!
The masses are the decisive element, they are the rock on which the final victory of the revolution will be built.
Capital is an historical necessity, but, so too, its grave digger, the socialist proletariat.
Without the collapse of capitalism the expropriation of the capitalist class is impossible.
Political power grows out of the barrel of a gun.
A revolution is not a dinner party, or writing an essay, or painting a picture, or doing embroidery.
quotes.source: Report on an Investigation of the Peasant Movement in Hunan (1927)

quotes.text: Let a hundred flowers blossom, let a hundred schools of thought contend.
quotes.source: On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People (1957)

quotes.text: All reactionaries are paper tigers.
Politics is war without bloodshed, while war is politics with bloodshed.
A single spark can start a prairie fire.
quotes.source: Letter of 5 January 1930, quoting an old Chinese saying

quotes.text: You young people, full of vigour and vitality, are in the bloom of life, like the sun at eight or nine in the morning.
quotes.source: Talk with Chinese students in Moscow (17 November 1957)

quotes.text: Our principle is that the Party commands the gun, and the gun must never be allowed to command the Party.
We thank Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin for giving us a weapon. This weapon is not a machine-gun, but Marxism-Leninism.
Serve the people.
Nothing is more precious than independence and freedom.
Vietnam has the right to be a free and independent country, and in fact it is so already.
Remember that the storm is a good opportunity for the pine and the cypress to show their strength and their stability.
quotes.source: Quoted in Hoang Van Chi, From Colonialism to Communism (1964)

quotes.text: At first, patriotism, not yet communism, led me to have confidence in Lenin, in the Third International.
quotes.source: The Path Which Led Me to Leninism (1960)

quotes.text: Journalists are also revolutionary soldiers. The pen and paper are their sharp weapons.
quotes.source: 3rd Congress of the Vietnam Journalists Association (1962)

quotes.text: In practice, the enemy has been making much more propaganda for us than we have ourselves.
Though frontiers and mountains stand between us, proletarians of the whole world come together as one family.
quotes.source: 3rd National Congress of the Vietnam Workers' Party (1960)

quotes.text: For the sake of ten years, plant trees; for the sake of a hundred years, cultivate people.
quotes.source: Saying adapted from the ancient Guanzi

quotes.text: Nothing is difficult; the only fear is a heart that is not steadfast. Dig through mountains and fill the seas: with resolve, it will be done.
quotes.source: Verse for youth volunteers, Bắc Kạn (30 March 1951)

quotes.text: Revolutionary morality consists in absolute loyalty to the Party and the people.
Hasta la victoria siempre!
In a revolution one wins or dies, if it is a real one.
At the risk of seeming ridiculous, let me say that the true revolutionary is guided by a great feeling of love.
Above all, try always to be able to feel deeply any injustice committed against any person in any part of the world.
Many will call me an adventurer, and that I am... only one of a different sort: one who risks his skin to prove his truths.
How close we could look into a bright future should two, three or many Vietnams flourish throughout the world.
Wherever death may surprise us, let it be welcome, provided that this, our battle cry, may have reached some receptive ear.
The guerrilla fighter is a social reformer.
The revolution is not an apple that falls when it is ripe. You have to make it fall.
quotes.source: Che Guevara Speaks: Selected Speeches and Writings (1967)

quotes.text: If you are capable of trembling with indignation each time that an injustice is committed anywhere in the world, we are comrades.
Condemn me, it does not matter: history will absolve me.
quotes.source: History Will Absolve Me, trial defense speech (1953)

quotes.text: A revolution is not a trail of roses… A revolution is a fight to the death between the future and the past.
quotes.source: Speech on the second anniversary of the revolution (2 January 1961)

quotes.text: Within the revolution, everything; against the revolution, nothing.
I am a Marxist-Leninist, and I will be a Marxist-Leninist until the last days of my life.
quotes.source: Speech on the anniversary of the Granma landing (2 December 1961)

quotes.text: Men do not shape destiny. Destiny produces the man for the hour.
The first duty of the revolutionaries is to tell the truth.
quotes.source: Speech at Camp Columbia, Havana (8 January 1959)

quotes.text: Revolutions are not exported, they are made by the people.
Capitalism produces beasts, socialism produces men.
They talk about the failure of socialism but where is the success of capitalism in Africa, Asia and Latin America?
Capitalism has neither the capacity, nor the moral, nor the ethics, nor the will to solve the problems of poverty.
